description: We are a team of motivated students from Tajikistan interested in space exploration, science, technology, and innovation. We are excited to participate in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, share ideas, learn new skills, and develop a creative project. We welcome people with different backgrounds and skills, especially in coding, design, research, data analysis, and communication.
summary:
Moon Base "Selena-0"

The Idea
You are the commander of a crew that has crash-landed on the Moon. A solar flare burned out your rocket's navigation board, and a micrometeorite cracked its fuel valve. But nearby stands an abandoned lunar base with oxygen tanks, seeds, a 3D printer, and the blueprints of your rocket.
Bring the base back to life: repair solar panels, fill modules with air, grow food, and mine water from crater ice. Every decision affects the others, because energy gives water and oxygen, and those give fuel. Engineer Mira and the robot Lunik will help you.
- The Goal
In the game, keep your crew alive, print the missing rocket parts from lunar soil, repair and refuel the rocket Zarya-1, and lift off to return home to Earth.
Along the way, you learn real science facts about the Moon. Mistakes aren't punishments, they're lessons.
Motto:Think, calculate, save your resources, and Earth will come closer.
details:
Our game is a 3D educational game for juniors, built in Unity and presented fully in English. The player controls a cosmonaut who explores a lunar base. Walking and jumping imitate the Moon’s low gravity, so movement feels close to real. The base includes the astronaut’s own room, a greenhouse, solar panels, a power center, a laboratory, and other modules that show why each part is important for living on the Moon. When the player starts a mission, the game switches from 3D to 2D. In this version there are two missions. In the Greenhouse mission, the player takes care of the plants that feed the crew through mini games. In the Laboratory mission, the player completes more mini games and a short quiz with facts about the Moon, so they learn something new while playing. The game saves progress for each game day, so players can come back and continue where they stopped. Most of the 3D models were made by our team, and we also used NASA’s official 3D model of the 70-meter Deep Space Network dish. New missions, such as power management or emergencies, can be added easily in the future.
